title: Integral and finite morphisms of spaces are etale local on the target
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Fix $P$ equal to integral or finite for scheme morphisms [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Say that $f$ is representable with property $P$ if, for every scheme $T$ and every map $T\to X$, the sheaf fibre product $Y\times_XT$ is a scheme and its projection to $T$ has $P$. Fibre products are [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For every representable surjective etale map $p:U\to X$ from a scheme $U$, $f$ is representable with property $P$ if and only if $Y\times_XU$ is a scheme and $Y\times_XU\to U$ has $P$. No quasi-compactness, separatedness, finite-type or Noetherian hypothesis on $S,X,Y,U$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 03ZQ (lemma-integral-local), equivalence (1) and (3), separately for integral and finite.

proof.text: If $f$ is representable with $P$, take the scheme test $T=U$ and the map $p:U\to X$ in the definition in the statement. This gives precisely the required scheme $Y\times_XU$ with its projection having $P$.

source.place: Tag 03ZQ (lemma-integral-local), direction (1) to (3), with the prescribed atlas

proof.text: Conversely suppose $W=Y\times_XU$ is a scheme and $W\to U$ has $P$. For either choice of $P$, the definition of integral and finite scheme morphisms says that $W\to U$ is affine. Apply the etale target criterion for affine space morphisms to the given representable surjective etale $U\to X$. It follows that $f$ is representable and affine.

Fix any scheme $T\to X$. Put $Z=Y\times_XT$ and $V=T\times_XU$. The affineness just proved, its base-change stability, and its scheme-target clause show that $Z$ is a scheme. The base-change assertion for etale covers shows that $V$ is a scheme and $q:V\to T$ is surjective etale. Pullback associativity identifies $Z\times_TV$ with $W\times_UV$ over $V$: both are the sheaf of triples $(y,t,u)$ whose three images in $X$ agree.

source.place: Tag 03ZQ (lemma-integral-local), (3) to (1), tested on an arbitrary scheme over the target

proof.text: The projection $W\times_UV\to V$ is integral if $P$ is integral, by stability of integral scheme morphisms under arbitrary base change; it is finite if $P$ is finite, by stability of finite scheme morphisms under arbitrary base change. Thus the preceding identification makes $Z\times_TV\to V$ a scheme morphism with $P$.

The singleton $\{q:V\to T\}$ is an etale covering of the terminal object $T$ of the small etale site of $T$, so the etale-to-fpqc covering lemma makes it an fpqc covering. Apply integral fpqc descent to $Z\to T$ in the integral case, and finite fpqc descent in the finite case. Their hypotheses hold because $Z,T,V$ are schemes and the unique base change has $P$. Hence $Z\to T$ has $P$. Since $T\to X$ was arbitrary, this proves representability with $P$. The covering lemma requires no quasi-compactness of $q$, so the argument introduces none of the excluded hypotheses.

lean.note: The two equivalences state the integral and finite choices separately. An existential scheme with a Yoneda pullback square expresses that the atlas fibre product is a scheme and its projection has the property. The existing scheme-test predicate IsRepresentableWith is used directly.
